# Management-System Safety Audit — Permit-to-Work (PTW) System
## Plant 3 Maintenance Shop — Issuance → Isolation → Sign-off → Close-out

**Audit reference:** PTW-P3-MS-01 · **Report date:** 6 July 2026
**Audit type:** Management-system (internal) audit — conformity assessment
**Method:** ISO 45001:2018 **clause 9.2** (internal audit) — scope → criteria → objective evidence → classified findings → conformity rating → corrective action → report
**Criteria:** ISO 45001:2018 **clause 8.1** (operational planning and control) **+** the organisation's own PTW procedure
**Jurisdiction:** United Kingdom (HSWA 1974 regime — PTW as a safe system of work) · **Risk matrix:** organisation 5×5 (multiply; Low 1–4 / Medium 5–9 / High 10–15 / Critical 16–25)
**Lead auditor:** Lead Auditor (ISO 45001 / ISO 19011, IRCA/CQI-registered) · **Audited function:** Plant 3 Maintenance Shop, 3-shift operation

> **Method vs criteria.** ISO 45001 **9.2** is the *method* — how this audit was planned and run. The audit was conducted *against* ISO 45001 **8.1** and the org PTW procedure — those are the *criteria*. 9.2 is never itself a pass/fail criterion here.

---

### Data protection & de-identification status

De-identification pass was completed **before** assessment. Identifiers detected in the raw evidence — issuer/holder names and signatures on the sampled permits, and worker names on the training matrix — were pseudonymised to stable **role labels**. The name↔label re-identification key is held in a **separate, access-controlled artifact** and is not reproduced in this report. No health data, injury categories, or sub-5 individual counts appear in this document; the numerals below (e.g. 4/12) are permit counts, not persons. **No personal identifier survives into any finding's evidence trail.**

## 1. Audit scope & boundary

| Element | Definition |
|---|---|
| **In scope** | The PTW system as the operational control governing maintenance work at the Plant 3 maintenance shop, across its four lifecycle stages: **issuance → isolation → sign-off → close-out**. Assessed across all **3 shifts**. |
| **Out of scope (boundary)** | **Hot-work permits are excluded** (declared boundary). Confined-space, working-at-height, and other permit classes not sampled are outside this audit and are not the subject of any finding here. |
| **Physical location** | Plant 3 maintenance shop. |

An audit is a **point-in-time sample, not a census**; findings generalise from the sampled evidence with that caveat and are conditioned on the sample described in §3.

---

## 2. Audit criteria (the clause-by-clause criteria set)

The PTW system is itself an **operational control** in the sense of ISO 45001 8.1.1 (a process established to meet OH&S requirements, operated to defined operating criteria). The criteria set the audit walked, mapped to ISO 45001 8.1 and the org PTW procedure:

| ID | Criterion (what "good" requires) | ISO 45001 8.1 mapping | Org PTW procedure |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C-1** | Permits issued only by **authorised, competent** persons under a documented procedure | 8.1.1 (control of the process to operating criteria; competent operation) | §3 issuance authorisation |
| **C-2** | Energy **isolation is verified and recorded** before work is authorised | 8.1.1 (operating criteria: hazardous energy isolated & confirmed) | isolation stage |
| **C-3** | The procedure **requires an independent isolation-verification step** before sign-off | 8.1.1 (defined operating criteria / process barrier) | §5 sign-off |
| **C-4** | Every permit is formally **closed out / signed back** on completion | 8.1.1 (control of the process end-state; return to service) | close-out stage |
| **C-5** | **Authorisers are competent** and in-date | 8.1.1 operated by competent persons (cross-ref 7.2 competence) | authoriser competence |
| **C-6** | **Live permits are controlled across shift handover** | 8.1.1 (control of the process across transitions) | shift-handover / open-permit control |

Corrective actions are additionally grounded in **8.1.2** (hierarchy of controls) and, where the procedure itself is changed, **8.1.3** (management of change).

---

## 3. Audit method & sampling basis

**Method:** ISO 45001 9.2 internal-audit loop, using triangulated evidence — document review, record sampling, direct observation, and role-based interview. Each criterion was assessed against the objective evidence; a criterion with absent evidence is recorded as a nonconformity or "insufficient evidence" — **never a silent pass**.

**Sample examined (the basis for every finding below):**

| Ref | Evidence | Nature | Sampling basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **E-1** | 12 issued permits across 3 shifts (issuers/holders by role) | Record sample | Point-in-time, all-shift spread; ~one working period |
| **E-2** | Org PTW procedure — §3 issuance authorisation present | Document review | Controlled document |
| **E-3** | Isolation-register extract | Record sample | Cross-checked against the 4 flagged permits |
| **E-4** | PTW procedure §5 — sign-off stage | Document review | Design of the sign-off barrier |
| **E-5** | Two interview summaries (Supervisor role; Issuer role) | Interview | 2 roles |
| **E-6** | PTW-authoriser training matrix (de-identified) | Record sample | All sampled issuers |
| **E-7** | Direct observation — one permit issuance + one shift handover | Observation | Single event |

**Sampling limitation (stated for defensibility):** the record sample is 12 permits and the handover evidence is a **single** observed event. Findings on isolation recording (F-2) and close-out (F-4) rest on a robust cross-shift sample; the handover finding (F-6) rests on one observation and is therefore treated as an observation, not a conformity assertion (§5).

## 4. Findings register (clause-by-clause — classified, evidence-traced, risk-rated)

*Classification scheme (ISO audit convention): Conformity · Nonconformity–Major (systemic failure / total absence of a required arrangement) · Nonconformity–Minor (isolated lapse against an otherwise-conforming arrangement) · Observation (conforming now, drift risk) · OFI (conforming, better practice available). Every nonconformity is risk-rated on the org 5×5.*

---

### F-1 · Issuance authorisation — **CONFORMITY**
- **Criterion:** C-1 (ISO 45001 8.1.1; org PTW procedure §3)
- **Objective evidence:** E-1 — **12/12** sampled permits carry an **authorised issuer role**; E-2 — procedure §3 (issuance authorisation) present and controlled; E-6 — all sampled issuers **in-date** on the authoriser matrix.
- **Assessment:** The issuance-authorisation arrangement is defined, documented, and consistently applied across all three shifts in the sample. Requirement met.
- **Risk rating:** n/a (conformity).

### F-2 · Isolation verification not recorded before authorisation — **NONCONFORMITY (MAJOR)**
- **Criterion:** C-2 (ISO 45001 8.1.1 — hazardous energy isolated and confirmed as an operating criterion)
- **Objective evidence:** E-1 — **4/12** permits signed off with **no recorded isolation check**; E-3 — isolation-register extract shows **corresponding gaps** against those same 4 permits.
- **Assessment:** In one third of the sample, the load-bearing energy-isolation barrier cannot be evidenced as having been verified before work was authorised. A ~33% cross-shift failure rate is **systemic, not isolated** — the recording control is failing across the population, not in one anomalous case. Whether isolation was physically performed cannot be confirmed from the records; from an audit-evidence standpoint conformity **cannot be asserted**.
- **Risk rating (org 5×5):** Severity **Major (4)** — uncontrolled release of hazardous energy (electrical / mechanical / stored) during maintenance can cause serious or fatal injury; Likelihood **Possible (3)** — recording gap on a third of the sample with no procedural verification barrier (see F-3), partially offset by competent authorisers (F-5). **Score 4 × 3 = 12 → HIGH.** Band action: *Intolerable — stop / additional controls before proceeding.*

### F-3 · Procedure lacks an independent isolation-verification step before sign-off — **NONCONFORMITY (MAJOR)**
- **Criterion:** C-3 (ISO 45001 8.1.1 — the management system must define the operating-criteria barrier)
- **Objective evidence:** E-4 — PTW procedure **§5 contains no independent isolation-verification step** before sign-off.
- **Assessment:** This is a **total absence of a required arrangement** in the system design and is the **systemic root** of F-2: the procedure permits sign-off on a single person's isolation with no independent cross-check, so there is no designed barrier to a single-point isolation error. A management system that relies on one person verifying their own isolation does not meet 8.1.1's operating-criteria-control requirement for a high-energy activity.
- **Risk rating (org 5×5):** Severity **Major (4)**; Likelihood **Possible (3)** — the barrier is absent system-wide, held down from higher only by demonstrated authoriser competence (F-6/E-6). **Score 4 × 3 = 12 → HIGH.** Band action: *Intolerable — stop / additional controls before proceeding.* *(Were authoriser competence not evidenced, this would escalate toward Critical.)*

### F-4 · Final close-out sign-back missing — **NONCONFORMITY (MINOR)**
- **Criterion:** C-4 (ISO 45001 8.1.1 — control of the process end-state / return to service)
- **Objective evidence:** E-1 — **2/12** permits lack the **final close-out sign-back**.
- **Assessment:** The close-out arrangement is otherwise in place and complied with (10/12); the two exceptions are an **isolated lapse against an otherwise-conforming arrangement** with no evidence the procedure itself is deficient — hence **minor**, not major. Risk is that a permit remains formally open, or plant is returned to service without a recorded confirmation that work is complete and isolations removed.
- **Risk rating (org 5×5):** Severity **Moderate (3)** — potential for plant returned to service in an unconfirmed state, or isolations left in place; Likelihood **Possible (3)** — 2/12 sample. **Score 3 × 3 = 9 → MEDIUM.** Band action: *Tolerable — reduce risk so far as is reasonably practicable (ALARP).*

### F-5 · Authoriser competence — **CONFORMITY**
- **Criterion:** C-5 (ISO 45001 8.1.1 operated by competent persons; cross-ref 7.2)
- **Objective evidence:** E-6 — authoriser training matrix (de-identified): **all sampled issuers in-date**.
- **Assessment:** Competence of the persons operating the PTW process is evidenced and current for the sample. Requirement met. *(This conformity is the compensating factor that holds F-2/F-3 at High rather than Critical.)*
- **Risk rating:** n/a (conformity).

### F-6 · Control of live permits across shift handover — **OBSERVATION (evidence insufficient to assert conformity)**
- **Criterion:** C-6 (ISO 45001 8.1.1 — control of the process across shift transitions)
- **Objective evidence:** E-7 — **one** observed permit issuance + shift handover (no deficiency seen in the observed event); E-5 — two role-based interview summaries (Supervisor, Issuer).
- **Assessment:** The single observed handover disclosed no nonconformity, but **one observation across a 3-shift operation is insufficient to assert conformity** of live-permit handover control. Given the open-permit exposure implied by F-4 (permits left un-signed-back), there is a **drift risk** that open permits are not systematically re-validated at shift change. Recorded as an **observation** with an associated improvement action, not a conformity and not (yet) a nonconformity.
- **Risk rating:** n/a (observation; optional — not scored pending a wider sample).

## 6. Risk-ranked nonconformity summary (org 5×5)

| Rank | Finding | Class | Likelihood × Severity | Score | Band | Band action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **F-3** Procedure has no independent isolation-verification step (systemic root) | Major NC | Possible (3) × Major (4) | **12** | **HIGH** | Intolerable — stop / additional controls before proceeding |
| 2 | **F-2** Isolation verification not recorded (4/12) | Major NC | Possible (3) × Major (4) | **12** | **HIGH** | Intolerable — stop / additional controls before proceeding |
| 3 | **F-4** Close-out sign-back missing (2/12) | Minor NC | Possible (3) × Moderate (3) | **9** | **MEDIUM** | Tolerable — reduce SFAIRP (ALARP) |

**Priority signal:** the two HIGH findings sit at the **isolation stage** — the load-bearing barrier of the whole PTW system. F-3 is the systemic cause; F-2 is its manifestation. The HIGH band action ("stop / additional controls before proceeding") requires an **immediate interim control** ahead of the permanent fix (CA-0, §7).

## 7. Corrective & preventive action plan (CAPA register)

*Every action is HoC-ranked (ISO 45001 8.1.2: Elimination → Substitution → Engineering → Administrative → PPE), SMART, role-owned, dated, linked to its finding, and carries a scheduled effectiveness review. Owners are role labels only. This validated register is the handoff artifact a CAPA-lifecycle process (e.g. `capa-manager`) would then track and close.*

| ID | Links to finding | Corrective / preventive action (SMART) | HoC tier | Owner (role) | Due | Effectiveness review |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **CA-0** *(interim)* | F-2, F-3 | **Effective immediately, pending CA-1/CA-2:** no PTW permit at Plant 3 maintenance shop is signed off until isolation has been **independently verified by a second competent person and that verification recorded on the permit**. Brief all authorised issuers/holders across all 3 shifts. **Measure:** interim instruction issued and acknowledged by 100% of authorised issuers within 48 h. | Administrative (interim barrier) | Maintenance Shop Supervisor (Plant 3) | **7 July 2026** | **21 July 2026** — confirm interim control in force across 3 shifts |
| **CA-1** | F-3 | **Revise PTW procedure §5** (via a managed change, ISO 45001 8.1.3) to require a **mandatory independent second-person isolation verification** — physical isolation confirmed by lock/tag and a **test-for-dead / try-to-start**, recorded on the permit — as a pre-condition of sign-off. **Measure:** revised §5 issued and controlled; independent-verification field present on the permit form; next 20-permit re-audit sample shows the step completed in 100% of cases. | Engineering + Administrative (physical isolation verification designed into the barrier) | HSE Manager (PTW procedure owner) | **15 August 2026** | **30 November 2026** — 20-permit re-audit |
| **CA-2** | F-2 | **Re-issue the permit template** with a **mandatory "isolation verified by (independent competent person)" field that cannot be left blank at sign-off** (form hard-stop / mistake-proofing), and brief all issuers/holders. **Measure:** new template in use across all 3 shifts; next 20-permit sample shows **0** missing isolation-verification records. | Engineering (mistake-proofing / hard-stop) + Administrative (briefing) | PTW System Owner / Authorised-Person coordinator | **22 August 2026** | **30 November 2026** — 20-permit re-audit |
| **CA-3** | F-4 | Add a **close-out verification gate**: a permit cannot be filed/closed without the **final sign-back** confirming work complete, isolations removed, and plant returned to service; end-of-shift supervisor countersignature. **Measure:** 100% of next 20-permit sample carry a completed close-out sign-back; monthly open-permit register shows zero permits closed without sign-back. **HoC justification:** close-out is inherently a verification/record control — higher-order elimination is not applicable; the highest reasonably practicable control is a mandatory form gate (engineering-style hard stop) plus countersign, which this action applies. | Administrative (justified — verification control, hard-stop applied) | Maintenance Shop Supervisor (Plant 3) | **29 August 2026** | **30 November 2026** — 20-permit re-audit |
| **CA-4** | F-6 | **Widen the sample and add control:** extend the audit of **live-permit shift handovers across all 3 shifts**, and add a **live-permit register to the shift-handover checklist** so every open permit is formally handed over and re-validated at each shift change. **Measure:** shift-handover checklist updated; a 2-week, 3-shift handover observation shows every open permit logged and re-validated. **HoC justification:** handover is a communication/verification control; strengthened by a documented register — higher-order controls not reasonably practicable for a shift-transition handover. | Administrative (justified) | Shift Supervisor | **12 September 2026** | **12 December 2026** — 3-shift handover re-observation |

**HoC integrity check:** no action is PPE-only; the two HIGH-band root fixes (CA-1, CA-2) embed a higher-order element (physical isolation verification / form hard-stop) rather than relying on procedure alone; the two administrative-only actions (CA-3, CA-4) each carry an explicit "higher-order not reasonably practicable" justification. No un-justified lower-order-only treatment remains.

---

## 8. Audit conclusion

The Plant 3 maintenance-shop PTW system is **partially conforming** to ISO 45001 clause 8.1 and the organisation's PTW procedure.

- **Conforms:** issuance authorisation (F-1) and authoriser competence (F-5) are defined, documented, and consistently evidenced across the sample. These are genuine strengths and are the compensating factors keeping the isolation-stage risk at HIGH rather than CRITICAL.
- **Does not conform:** the **isolation stage — the load-bearing barrier of the whole system — is systemically deficient.** The procedure designs in no independent isolation-verification step (**F-3, major, HIGH**) and, consistent with that gap, one third of the sampled permits carry no recorded isolation check (**F-2, major, HIGH**). A minor close-out lapse (**F-4, medium**) and an unproven handover control (**F-6, observation**) compound the exposure at the two ends of the permit lifecycle.
- **Overall verdict:** the PTW system **cannot presently be relied upon** as an adequate operational control for hazardous-energy maintenance work until the two HIGH nonconformities are corrected. The interim control (**CA-0**) must be in force immediately; the permanent fixes (**CA-1, CA-2**) close the systemic gap; **CA-3/CA-4** address the residual lifecycle weaknesses. Re-audit of a fresh 20-permit sample at the scheduled effectiveness-review dates will confirm closure.

**Boundary reminder:** hot-work permits were excluded from this audit; this conclusion makes no statement about them.

## 9. Assurance, limitations & competent-person review

- **Assurance pass applied:** an ISO 45001 9.2 / ISO 19011 lead-auditor review lens was applied to this report — every finding traced to objective evidence against a named criterion, each classification tested (major vs minor vs observation), every nonconformity risk-rated, and the CAPA register checked for a clean lifecycle handoff. This assurance step is **decision-support; it precedes and does not replace** the human competent-person sign-off, and it does **not** constitute approval by a competent person.
- **Sampling limitation:** conclusions rest on a 12-permit cross-shift sample, an isolation-register extract, two role-based interviews, the authoriser matrix, and one observed event. Findings generalise from that sample with the stated caveats; the handover finding (F-6) is explicitly evidence-limited.
- **Risk scoring:** bands were derived by applying the organisation's locked 5×5 calibration (multiply; Low 1–4 / Medium 5–9 / High 10–15 / Critical 16–25). In a full engine run these figures are produced deterministically by the shared `risk_matrix` component; they are reproduced here against that same calibration.

> **Disclaimer — decision-support only.** This audit report is decision-support, not legal advice and not a certification statement. It **must be reviewed and signed off by a competent person** (a qualified HSE lead/auditor familiar with the site and the applicable UK legislation) before it is relied upon or acted on. The corrective actions, owners, and dates are proposed for that competent person's confirmation. Assessment of energy-isolation adequacy in particular requires competent on-site verification.
